INNOVATION
AND IMPACT
©USAID | Global Health
Leveraging the Private Sector for the COVID-19 Response Concept Note
Vaccine Information & Community Engagement through Facebook and
WhatsApp
Summary
Leverage the network, reach, and influence of Facebook and its associated 1:1 communication channels
like WhatsApp to improve the distribution of accurate COVID-19 information, spark demand for the
COVID vaccine, and create positive information campaigns to reduce vaccine hesitancy.
Problem Statement
Many countries are facing a high level of COVID-19 vaccine hesitancy, rampant mis or disinformation
about COVID in general, and related to its vaccines, cures, treatments, or the origins of the virus, and
mistrust in public health agencies or governments. In many places, these issues are resulting in
insufficient demand for the COVID vaccine, improper use of masks, limited social distancing, and low
levels of testing, reporting, or quarantining. Combined, these challenges can significantly impede a
sub-national, national, and global response to COVID.
Proposal
Use Facebook's COVID Vaccine Information Center, ad campaigns, Data for Good program, and
WhatsApp chatbots to disseminate accurate and timely information regarding COVID at the sub-national
level, promote positive ad and media public health campaigns, and conduct robust M&E on the success
of these efforts. These tools can help Ministries of Health and other government departments leverage
the power of Facebook's multiple platforms and wide audience to enhance community engagement,
generate demand for the COVID vaccine, and distribute information that can lead to appropriate action.
Main offerings
Facebook has engaged in many activities to combat COVID-19 and further the spread of accurate and
timely information about the disease. One initiative included making the WHO website accessible to
users in low-and-middle-income countries (LMICs) without incurring data charges. Other initiatives that
Facebook offers or can offer LMIC governments include:
• Connecting people to reliable information about COVID-19 vaccines, through:
• Use of the COVID Information Center, which is live in over 200 countries and has been
translated into over 70 languages. This center enables Facebook users to get local
information at scale by showcasing information from local, national, regional and global
health authorities.

• Delivery of ad credits and media space to Ministries of Health or other public health
organizations that are putting out health messaging. So far, Facebook has given more
than $30 million in ad credits to help governments, NGOs, and other organizations reach
people with COVID-19 vaccine information and other important messages. These
information campaigns resulted in an estimated 10 billion ad impressions globally.
• A sample COVID-19 vaccine campaign structure for a country can include several
stages, beginning with awareness:
• Phase 1: Build vaccine confidence amongst the general public by
distributing the national vaccine rollout plan, facts about vaccine safety,
ingredients, and population prioritization
• Phase 2: Alert high-risk group 60+ in four regions by sending information
about vaccine availability, registration sites, and vaccination locations
• Phase 3: Register priority group for vaccinations by driving registrations
on MoH or other website
• Phase 4: Remind and reinforce behavior by sending reminders about
registrations, vaccination dates, and locations
Facebook can work with a country to tailor messages for the citizens of that country,
such as encouraging vaccine registrations, social distancing, wearing masks, etc. This
approach is similar to what Facebook has done in the past for certain countries by
reminding individuals in a country to vote around the time of elections.
• Conducting M&E to help drive decision-making and policy-making in LMICs:
• Facebook can support ad evaluations to help decision-makers see how effective their
advertisement campaigns and messages are at encouraging individuals to display
health-seeking behavior such as mask-wearing or vaccine registrations.
Facebook'sData for Good program has been implementing a COVID survey for over a
year now with over 200 countries, collecting incredibly valuable information around the
key drivers of vaccine hesitancy, mask usage, and uptake of behaviors. See visualizations
nere.
• Leveraging WhatsApp for push messaging:
• Given the ubiquity of WhatsApp in LMICs, Facebook has worked with the WHO and
governments to access their API, working with developer partners to create chatbots for
governments to promote health-related content.
• For example, Facebook worked with the Ministry of Health in Buenos Aires,
Argentina to create a chatbot around COVID testing availability and COVID
vaccines, so users receive a notification that gives them a phone number to get
MoH information on WhatsApp and a number to text to receive information.
This approach enables user-initiated messaging and empowers citizens to take
control over their own health in a secured and end-to-end encrypted platform.

Since the start of the pandemic, WhatsApp has partnered with more than 150 national,
state, and local governments, and with organizations like WHO and UNICEF, on COVID-19
helplines to connect over 2 billion users to accurate information and resources. Over 3
billion messages have been sent across these global helplines in the past year.
As the pandemic enters a new phase in many countries, governments are using these
helplines to connect citizens privately to accurate vaccine information and registration,
in countries such as Indonesia, South Africa, Argentina, Brazil, and India. In Indonesia,
500,000 medical workers registered for their vaccine appointments on this service in its
first 5 days.
WhatsApp wants to help governments and international organizations connect as many
people around the world to vaccine information and services as possible, especially
those in hard-to-reach places or in marginalized groups. They have also waived the fees
that come from sending messages through the WhatsApp Business API.
Timeline and Cost
Most of these activities are self-serve and can begin anytime. At this time, Facebook does not have an
inbound request service.
